title: Derivative of a squared profile pair
statement: Let $U$ be the Gaussian isoperimetric profile and $Q$ the total Gaussian quantile. For $a,t,k\in\mathbb R$ with $a+t,a-t\in(0,1)$, the function $x\mapsto U(a+x)^2+kU(a-x)^2$ is differentiable at $t$, with derivative $-2U(a+t)Q(a+t)+2kU(a-t)Q(a-t)$.
replaced: Let $\Phi$ and $\varphi$ be the standard Gaussian distribution function and density, and put $Q=\Phi^{-1}$ and $I(p)=\varphi(Q(p))$ for $0<p<1$. If $a,t,k\in\mathbb R$ and $a\pm t\in(0,1)$, then the derivative of $x\mapsto I(a+x)^2+kI(a-x)^2$ at $t$ is $-2I(a+t)Q(a+t)+2kI(a-t)Q(a-t)$.
